edge_explainer: The screen premise (cheap 88%-GM FCF machine, -46% off its high, new-CEO refresh) is factually true and analytically inverted. Slow growth was never the problem: GAAP operating income went $904.2M (2020) -> $831.1M (2025) on +32% revenue, a -13.3pp margin slide, and cash from operations has not grown since 2021. The multiple has been de-rating rationally for six years because earnings power stopped growing in 2019; 2026 is simply the year the revenue line converged on the profit line. The decisive Mode-B test is competitive and unambiguous: in the June-2026 quarter CHKP product revenue fell 14.0% and the maintenance annuity fell 3.3% (its first-ever decline) while Fortinet - the closest structural comparable, same buyer, same refresh calendar, lapping the same strong comp - grew total revenue +25.6% and Palo Alto +31.2%. The firewall refresh up-cycle is ON and Check Point is losing it, which refutes both available bull defences (industry air-pocket; tough comp) simultaneously. Probability-weighted FV $125.2 vs $122.97 spot = +1.8pp, i.e. the -47.5% de-rate has already carried the price to fair-for-the-trajectory. Long has no edge; short is correct-diagnosis-uninvestable ($2.2B net cash = 18% of cap, 10.2% FCF yield on EV, a fresh $2B authorisation retiring ~10%/yr of float, a 24% founder holder, and a take-private tail at 10x EV/FCF). The deliverable is the exclusion of the cohort's #1-ranked tier-1 name.

honesty_finding.note: Nothing is hidden - every datum is in the tables and this court rebuilt all of it. What diverges is the marketed frame, through three channels at once. (1) METRIC RETIREMENT: Calculated Billings LED the Q4-2025 highlights (+8% Q4, +9% FY) and is absent from both the Q1-2026 and Q2-2026 releases; Products & Licenses was a highlight bullet at +12% and is absent at -14%. Both retirements run the same direction; the one metric retained (RPO) is the one still positive. Reconstructed from the balance sheets, 1H-2026 calculated billings = -0.7% YoY vs FY2025 +9%, a ~10pp swing - approximate because acquired deferred revenue is written down in purchase accounting, but the direction is not in doubt, and the company retired the metric rather than print it. (2) SUBSIDY-CARRIED OPERATING LINE: a new Israeli R&D law enacted 2026-03-30 was booked as a $28M reduction of Q2 R&D expense ($55M in 1H), disclosed only in an income-statement footnote and NOT carved out of the marketed '39 percent' non-GAAP operating margin. Ex-grant, Q2 non-GAAP operating income is -14.5% YoY (not -4.2%) and the margin is 34.4% (not 38.6%) vs 40.8% a year ago; the grant is now ~11% of non-GAAP operating income and is a politically revocable sovereign subsidy. (3) MANUFACTURED EPS GROWTH: headline non-GAAP EPS +7.6% decomposes to non-GAAP net income +0.8% on a -6.3% share count, i.e. essentially 100% buyback - and that +0.8% is itself entirely the $28M grant plus $13.0M of incremental financial income earned on the $2B of BORROWED convert proceeds. Strip both and non-GAAP net income is ~-15%. Against all of that the CEO's quote reads 'results in line with our expectations while strengthening our foundation for sustainable growth'. Not a disclosure violation; the softer and more common failure - a marketed takeaway constructed by retiring the metrics that turned, letting a one-off subsidy carry the operating line, and letting debt-funded buyback carry the per-share line.

israel_domicile.pfic: NOT a PFIC - CONFIRMED. Non-obvious: on a BOOK basis the asset test looks alarming ($4,203M cash+securities / $7,512M total assets = 56% passive, above the 50% threshold), but a publicly traded foreign corporation applies the test on FAIR MARKET VALUE, under which goodwill and going-concern value are active. FMV of assets ~= $12.52B market cap + $4.78B liabilities = $17.3B; passive $4.20B = 24%. Income test clean by a wide margin (~$2.78B active revenue vs ~$164M/yr financial income = ~6% passive). No QEF or mark-to-market election, no Form 8621. Clean for the taxable book.
israel_domicile.withholding_tax: Not currently binding. CHKP pays no dividend and never has; all shareholder return is buyback. If a dividend were initiated, distributions out of Preferred / Technological Preferred Enterprise income carry Israeli withholding of 15% or 20% (20-F Taxation), treaty-reducible and creditable via Form 1116. The all-buyback policy is in fact the tax-efficient structure for this household; a dividend initiation would be a mild negative, not a positive.
israel_domicile.geopolitical_tail: Real, unhedgeable, low-probability, and NOT the reason to pass. HQ Tel Aviv, R&D concentrated in Israel, material reserve-duty exposure in any regional escalation; the company traded through October 2023 without operational impairment, so the base rate of permanent damage is low. The newer and more specific sovereign exposure is the March-2026 Israeli R&D credit, now ~11% of non-GAAP operating income and subject to budget revision. Size for the tail, do not underwrite it as the thesis. Not load-bearing here - the name fails on competitive grounds long before geopolitics matters.

ai_complex_conflict.statement: Courted explicitly against the frozen house call AI-BREAK|2027-12-31 @ 0.45 rather than averaged away. CHKP sells network security into enterprise IT budgets: no datacenter capex leverage, no GPU supply chain, no hyperscaler concentration. Its AI content is marketing positioning plus small tuck-ins (Lakera, Cyata). An entry would NOT require the AI cycle holding, and the -47.5% de-rate is idiosyncratic and competitive rather than AI-cycle-driven - making CHKP one of the few large-cap tech assets whose drawdown is uncorrelated with that call, against the household's ~$5.2M / 26% AI-complex exposure. This does NOT rescue the name: an AI-uncorrelated business that is losing share and whose operating income has fallen for six years is still losing share. The diversification property moved the score by roughly half a point, no more.
